# `Q-5-53` — Project Does Not Declare a Quarto Version

> `_quarto.yml` has no `quarto-required` key, so the project is
> presumed to be a Quarto 1 project.

## What this means

Quarto 2 is not fully backwards compatible with Quarto 1, so a project
says which major version it is written for with `quarto-required` in
`_quarto.yml`. This project's `_quarto.yml` has no such line.

Quarto 1 releases that predate Quarto 2 cannot be changed, so a
`_quarto.yml` without the declaration might belong to a project written
for any of them. Quarto 2 presumes it is a Quarto 1 project. It still
renders the project, and reports this warning once per render.

## How to fix it

If the project is meant for Quarto 2, add one line to `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
quarto-required: "^2"
```

Quarto 1 (version 1.4 and later) then refuses to render the project,
instead of rendering it with different results.

Only the project's own `_quarto.yml` counts. The line has no effect in
a profile file, `_quarto.yml.local`, `_metadata.yml`, a document's
front matter or `-M`. See
[Declaring the Quarto version of a project](../../guides/projects/quarto-version.qmd).

If the project is a Quarto 1 project that you render with Quarto 2 on
purpose, silence the warning in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-5-53:
    level: off
    reason: "a Quarto 1 project we render with both versions"
```
